Consider the affine transformation $T,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What would be the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that for any affine transformation 

$$
T:u⟶Au+b,
$$

where $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and $u$ and $b$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors, we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., when $det(A)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., when $det(A)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $A$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $A$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a point on the plane.

With that in mind, let's examine our transformation.

Notice that the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is a zero matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, $T$ is non-invertible, and the image of the triangle under the action of $T$ is a point on the plane.
